name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 partisan lean in a Democratic-held Northern Virginia seat
Overwhelming money gap: Walkinshaw raised $2.8M plus $2.7M outside support vs Purves' $31K

model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean, Walkinshaw's incumbency, and a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising advantage leave Purves without a visible path; prediction markets and district fundamentals point to the same comfortable incumbent win.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race or a late surge of Republican outside spending would be the main signal to revisit this rating.

overview:
Virginia's 11th District, in the Democratic-leaning inner suburbs of Northern Virginia, has an 18-point partisan edge toward Democrats. James Walkinshaw, the Democratic incumbent, faces Republican Arthur Purves and a Green Party candidate in November. The structural picture strongly favors the incumbent: district lean, incumbency, and a large financial advantage all point the same direction.

Walkinshaw has raised about $2.8 million with roughly $1 million on hand, backed by about $2.7 million in outside support, while Purves has raised about $31,000 with no meaningful outside backing. No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, but prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 97 percent. The expected margin sits in the mid-20s, and the race is rated Safe Democratic.
